##### 1.1 Model

The equations below present inflation and output in the New Keynesian model which you have studied in the lectures, but with a slight change. The first term

1

1 Yt = EtYt+1 − (it − Etπt+1). (1) σ

πt = βEtπt+1 + κYt + μt, (2)

However, the Taylor rule is different than in the lectures and previous assignments: the nominal interest rate now reacts to lagged values of inflation and output rather than to expectations.

i

it = φπ πt−1 + φy yt−1 + t, (3) Finally, as you see in the above equations, there are two shocks, one to **infla-**

i

**tion** (μt) and one to the **nominal interest rate** ( t). The shock to the nominal interest rate is white noise (no auto-correlation and normally distributed with mean zero). However, the shock to inflation follows an AR(1) process that can be described by

μ

μt = ρμμt−1 + t , (4)

μ

with t a white noise term (random variable with no autocorrleation and normally distributed with mean zero), and ρμ the auto-correlation coefficient of the shock μt. Given that past inflation and past output gap show up in the Taylor rule, these variables are state variables. Moreover, the 2 white noise terms are also state variables, and so is the lagged value of the autorcorrelated shock μ. The minimum state variable solution will therefore look like this:

μ i zt = Cμμt−1 + Cy yt−1 + Cπ πt−1 + Cμ t + Ci t (5)

For some vectors of coefficients Cμ, Cy , Cπ , Cμ and Ci. Unless otherwise stated, use the following values for the parameters in the model
